issues.legal_issue: A co-owner who has not made a timely written objection seeking a reference cannot obtain enhanced compensation through a reference sought by another co-owner for that co-owner’s share.
material_facts: Land was acquired and compensation was apportioned among the co-owners, with each receiving a separate share.
Another co-owner sought a reference and obtained enhanced compensation.
The claimant did not establish that she had made her own timely written application seeking a reference.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to enhanced compensation based on the reference sought by the other co-owner, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 18(1) and 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, a written application within the prescribed limitation is a condition precedent to a reference; the civil court’s jurisdiction to determine higher compensation depends on a valid reference. A reference sought by one co-owner for that co-owner’s share is not an application on behalf of all co-owners. Sections 53 and 30 do not make Order 1, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure applicable to override the Act’s inconsistent reference procedure; the CPC applies to trial procedure after a valid reference. The judgment cites no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference_: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired for a public purpose and a reference to a civil court for determination of compensation.
predicates.compensation_apportioned_separately: The compensation was allocated to the co-owners as separate shares.
predicates.another_coowner_sought_reference_for_own: A co-owner sought a reference concerning that co-owner’s own share.
predicates.claimant_made_no_timely_written_objectio: The claimant did not make a timely written application objecting to the compensation and seeking a reference.
predicates.claimant_cannot_receive_enhancement_base: The claimant cannot obtain enhanced compensation solely on the basis of another co-owner’s reference.

issues.definition: When compensation is apportioned separately in a land acquisition compensation reference case, another co-owner seeks a reference for their own share, and the claimant made no timely written objection, the claimant cannot receive enhancement based on that other co-owner’s reference.
